<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-unit.object.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via realtimeService (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via buildDriverOptions (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/examples.mdx`  _(via buildHookApi (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via buildDriverOptions (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet), buildSession (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via buildDriverOptions (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/realtime-protocol.mdx`  _(via publishDataEvent (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via cascadeDeleteRelations (literal, a string literal in DeleteAndAggregateFacet))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-unit.object.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4609c48962b94289fe0ceeb7dd0076e2b02b0790` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `76aa9bba50fd93a6c5a2654ebc7a5199203fa5eb` — the merge of head `5ebea45947f3aa30f0c874a2f361345598f81f27` into base `4609c48962b94289fe0ceeb7dd0076e2b02b0790`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 76aa9bba50fd93a6c5a2654ebc7a5199203fa5eb && git checkout 76aa9bba50fd93a6c5a2654ebc7a5199203fa5eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4609c48962b94289fe0ceeb7dd0076e2b02b0790 5ebea45947f3aa30f0c874a2f361345598f81f27 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4609c48962b94289fe0ceeb7dd0076e2b02b0790 && git merge --no-ff 5ebea45947f3aa30f0c874a2f361345598f81f27

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4609c48962b94289fe0ceeb7dd0076e2b02b0790
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4609c48962b94289fe0ceeb7dd0076e2b02b0790` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review brief — PR #35930 @ `5ebea45947f3aa30f0c874a2f361345598f81f27` (card #35812)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35812: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #35930: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `5ebea45947f3aa30f0c874a2f361345598f81f27`

⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — `reviewFace` returns no `hits` on this PR's file list; the review is owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration, and the claim (7047043860, amended 7048707723) sets it at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER because a delete door widens. Treat as `hits` the widened door and its gate: packages/objectql/src/validation/unit-code-membership.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

Points the seat puts in front of you explicitly (judge them in ③, do not take the seat's view as the answer):
  · The unit deletes run with system authority (a sudo-shaped context keeping the caller's userId and transaction, tenantId set to the organization being deleted), not with the caller's authority as other cascade children do. The stated reason: no permission set grants a unit delete, so the gate is the caller's authority over the organization row; the cited precedent is plugin-auth's removeOrganizationAuthStructure. Try to break it: can any caller reach the removal without an admitted organization delete, or reach another organization's units?
  · The exemption must be keyed on engine-internal provenance a caller cannot forge (the card body). Judge whether `referentialCascadeDelete === true && isOrganizationUnitRemoval(...)` holds that against every other delete path: user, system, automation, by id, batched, a hook's delete during the cascade, and a forged cascade token.
  · Atomicity: an organization delete refused for another owned row removes no unit.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f6f2f87a-1f68-5b6b-ba36-b37fd0636732/scratchpad/d7d/pr-35930/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5ebea45947f3aa30f0c874a2f361345598f81f27`

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, widened (right).** `delete('sys_organization', by id)` of an organization whose only tenant-owned rows are `sys_unit` rows was 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED` and is now admitted, removing those units. This is ruling 7035627429 option B, word for word.

An organization holding any other record is still refused, and the refusal names only that record.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35812-org-delete-removes-units.md` is `patch` for `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/plugin-security`, and carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, the same two lines as the PR body. Patch is right for objectql: a fix that restores a door #35805 closed by accident, with no public signature change. The widening is declared and described in the "Declared behaviour change" paragraph, and that paragraph matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Seat point 1 — unit deletes run with system authority. Accepted.**
- The context is `{ ...referenceCheckContext(context), tenantId: String(organizationId) }`: the caller's transaction and `userId` kept, `isSystem: true`, tenant set to the deleted organization.
- The cited precedent is real and reads as cited: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.ts` `removeOrganizationAuthStructure` deletes teams, team members and grants under `SYSTEM_CTX` inside the request's transaction.
- Caller authority cannot serve here: `organization_admin` grants no delete on `sys_unit`, so a caller-authority delete would be refused for every caller and the ruling could not be met.
- Reach without an admitted organization delete: none found. `removeOrganizationUnits` is module-private with one call site, the end of `walkReferencingRelations` under `object === ORGANIZATION_OBJECT`. That walk is reached only from `cascadeDeleteRelations`, called only from `delete()`'s executor, which runs after the middleware chain (the authorization gate), after the by-id pre-image read under the caller's scope (a missing or unreadable organization row is `recordNotFound` before the cascade), and after `beforeDelete`. A predicate delete of `sys_organization` is refused earlier (`organizationPredicateDeleteRefusal`), so only a by-id delete arrives.
- Reach into another organization's units: none found. The ids come from one read with `where: { [tenantField]: organizationId }`, and both the read and the deletes carry `tenantId` of that same organization. The unit-test and real-stack pins both keep the other organization's unit.
- One consequence the seat should know: a `sys_unit` or `*` delete hook that writes through `ctx.api` during the removal writes as system with the caller's `userId`. That is the same posture as the plugin-auth precedent; hooks are server code.

**Seat point 2 — provenance a caller cannot forge. Holds.**
- The gate is `referentialCascadeDelete === true && isOrganizationUnitRemoval(this.cascadeIssuedDeletes.getStore())`. The first half means THIS call claimed the ambient token (`claimReferentialCascadeDelete` matches object and exact id, then sets `claimed`). The second half means that token object is in `organizationUnitRemovals`, a module-private `WeakSet` only `removeOrganizationUnits` adds to.
- User, system writer, automation run, by id: no ambient token, so no claim: refused.
- Batched (`multi`, `$in`): the removal issues by-id tokens only; a predicate never matches an `id` token (`typeof id === 'object'`): refused.
- A hook's delete during the cascade: the organization's `beforeDelete` runs before any token exists; a unit's own hook runs after its token is claimed, so a delete of the same unit, a sibling or a batch claims nothing: refused. The claim precedes every middleware and hook of the unit delete; between `cascadeIssuedDeletes.run` and the claim only engine option-lowering runs.
- A forged token entered through the engine's TS-private `cascadeIssuedDeletes` store: claimed, but not in the `WeakSet`: refused. Pinned, and the dev's ablation a4 shows the pin is the one that catches a claim-only gate.
- Nothing a request or an `ExecutionContext` carries is read by the gate.

**Seat point 3 — atomicity. Holds for refusals; one declared degrade.**
- `refuseOrganizationDeleteWhileOwned` runs for every root id before the first relation, every `restrict` in the relation loop throws before the removal, and the removal is the last statement of the walk. A refused organization delete therefore removes no unit, on any driver. Pinned in both suites (`store.writes` is empty).
- A failure AFTER the removal (the organization row's own `driver.delete`, an aborting `afterDelete`) rolls the units back wherever the plan is `'atomic'`, which it is whenever `sys_unit` sits on the default driver, because its tenant column is itself a relation `planCascadeAtomicity` counts. On a driver without transactions the units stay removed while the organization lives. That is ADR-0119 D1's declared degrade, shared by every cascade and by the plugin-auth path ("the refusals are the guarantee"). Not a finding of this PR; the seat may want it written into the ADR-0158 note.
- A unit inserted by another writer between the removal's read and the organization row's delete is left naming a deleted organization. The same window exists for every owned row the refusal counts; not new here.

**SQL push-down.** `removeOrganizationUnits` reads the organization's unit ids and deletes each by id. A reason is given in its docblock: each unit goes through the public `delete()` under a token naming exactly that unit, so hooks, audit and events are a cascade child's, and the provenance is per row. The id set is inherent in that mechanism, and an organization's units are tens of rows. Accepted; no finding.

**Dev flags and open questions.**
- "Unit deletes run with system authority, dev recommends accept": answered above, accepted.
- "An OI11 ADR note is owed on landing": true, and the claim forbids `docs/adr/**` here. ADR-0158 on `main` still says a deleted code "is never created again" with no exemption. See N4.
- "Out of scope, not filed: the two comments still say every context": stale. The head's second commit fixed both. See N3.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/objectql/src/validation/unit-code-membership.ts` (hits).** Holds. The function stays a pure refusal and takes the verdict as a boolean, so the membership module learns nothing about cascades. The docblock's three sentences ("the engine's own answer", "claimed once", "anyone else's delete while the organization's delete is in flight is refused") each match the call site and `claimReferentialCascadeDelete`. Against ADR-0158 Open item 11: the hazard is a code created again with another meaning inside an organization; a deleted organization creates nothing, so the exemption does not reopen it. L1's "old rows keep their code" is untouched: rows that outlive the organization keep the code and show it without a label.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` (hits).** Holds. The refusal moved from the top of `delete()` to just after the cascade claim, which it must follow to read it. Every statement between the two positions either throws or lowers options; none returns, writes, or runs caller code, so "before any middleware or hook" is still true. See N1.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts` (hits).** Holds. Placement, provenance and tenant scoping are judged in ③.
